title: RAW_UNREVIEWED: two fever-class doses and a separate carried-plant route are stated as similar outcomes
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_UNSELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In the tricoccum/scorpiuron passage of Pliny XXII.29 (Bostock/Riley 1856 English layer), four seed grains in drink are said to cure quartan fever and three to cure tertian; the text then says a similar effect comes from carrying the plant three times around the patient and laying it under the head. This is a speculative route-and-dose contrast: retain the class-specific counts and the distinct patient-centered handling sequence without collapsing them into one dosing event. The historical efficacy is not verified and no target word is proposed.

source_evidence.quote: Four [page 415] grains of the seed, taken in drink, are said to be a cure for the quartan fever, and three for the tertian; a similar effect being produced by carrying the plant three times round the patient, and then laying it under his head.

design.falsifier: The distinction fails if the source does not assign the different counts to the named fever classes or does not separately describe the carried-plant route as producing a similar effect.
